blocks.text: Northstar

Country Hills uses Northstar for their POS systems in their Proshop,  Ridge Bar (eatery), and Spike Lounge. As is the case with the CWC, Country Hills should try to contact Northstar for support, but there are a few issues that can be dealt with remotely:
Common Issues
POS link doesn’t work/redirects to the wrong POS: Clear the cache/cookies, ensure
the POS link points to the proper POS link from Northstar
POS prints to the same printer: Check to see the POS link points to the right POS
(example: Kitchen Right POS displays Links Bar POS)

Onboarding Process - Active Directory
Have the hiring manager/original ticket creator fill in the New User Request Form.
Make sure that the user provides as much detail as possible. This includes any other third-party applications, distribution lists, security groups, etc.

Determine if the user is created in Admin 365 or in Active Directory. If the user is created in AD always perform changes on AD even if the same options exist in Admin 365 (example: resetting passwords).
Create the new user in the proper folder (this can either be a general “Users” folder or a folder specifically for their department).
For Country Hills, the name format is
[firstname].[lastname]@countryhills.ab.ca
John Doe → john.doe@countryhills.ab.ca

If applicable, you can use a departing user as a template for the new user (ask the ticket creator beforehand). Add the user’s job title in “Description” if other users in the company have their job title listed as well.
When creating a user, make sure to use the @countryhills.ab.ca email, never .local unless stated otherwise. In “Attributes”, under proxyaddress, add the user’s new email address:
Example: SMTP:john.doe@countryhills.ab.ca

Add the new user into the relevant share folders and security groups that the ticket creator did not add in the New User Request Form. Use the DeltaSync file located in the Desktop to push the newly created user.
Make sure to use the Secret Sharing system from Club Support when sending passwords!
https://csms.clubsupportinc.com/secrets
Onboarding Process - Microsoft 365
Log in to Microsoft 365 with the csupport@countryhills.ab.ca account.

Find the newly created user and under Licenses, grant the license (if any) requested by the ticket creator, which should be outlined in the New User Request Form. If a license is required, send an email to “Licenses@clubsupportinc.com” under this format:

	Subject: Add (1/2/etc.) license to Country Hills

Body:

	License is for:

	User Requesting License (username@countryhills.ab.ca)
Exchange Online/Business Standard Monthly/Yearly Commit
Requested by
Manager/Controller		Ticket No.

Depending on the club, mailbox delegation, distribution lists, and other 365-exclusive groups should also be assigned in Exchange. To do so, go to “Exchange”, then depending on the mailbox, grant the proper permissions. For example, if you want to delegate the shared mailbox “Catering” to the user, go to the catering mailbox, and add the new user under the “Read and Manage” permissions.

Outlook usually adds the inbox to the user’s mailbox automatically, but if this doesn’t occur, you can add the mailbox manually in Outlook. To do this, right-click the account name in the left folder pane, select Add shared folder or mailbox, enter the mailbox address.

tabs.tab: Proper Server Shutdown and Startup Procedure

blocks.text: Consult with Yurii/Stan and any managers before doing any server shutdowns and startups. They are in charge of the regularly scheduled server reboots for most of the clubs. If they are unavailable, contact Kosta as we do not reboot servers without prior consent. If a shutdown is required, here is a general guideline to maintain connectivity:
Notify users and departments of the downtime and provide an accurate timeframe on when services can be fully up and running again.
Schedule the downtime after hours (Usually 10:00 PM to 4:00 AM local time) to prevent any issues in the future.
Shutdown and/or restart the servers as required and log everything that occurs.
Offboarding Process - Active Directory
Club Support Policy dictates that we rarely, if ever delete accounts in systems once created. Permissions and security group memberships in AD are generally left intact.

Reset the password to ensure that the user cannot sign-in with their previous credentials. Afterwards, right click the user to be offboarded, and press “Disable” if requested. If any changes are done, make sure to run the DeltaSync script on the desktop.
Offboarding Process - Microsoft 365
The offboarding process differs from club to club, so double check the ticket as the creator will usually include what needs to be taken off and what needs to be retained

Log in to the 365 portal with csupport@countryhills.ab.ca and find the user to be offboarded. To disallow the user from signing back in, press both “Block Sign-in” and “Sign Out Of All Sessions” to remove the user.

To unlicense a user, go to “Licenses” and remove their Microsoft 365 Basic/Standard license to remove their Outlook and Word license. If the license isn’t immediately being transferred to another user, you can remove the license by emailing Licenses@clubsupportinc.com
Subject: Remove (1/2/etc.) license in Country Hills

In Exchange, go to the user to be offboarded, and convert their mailbox into a shared mailbox. If Read Access, Send, or Send As access is requested by the ticket creator, this is also done in Exchange. Email forwarding is also done in Exchange if requested by the ticket creator.
New PC / Laptop Setup Guide
STEP 1 – GATHER IMPORTANT INFORMATION
Before replacing the old PC/laptop, collect the following information
Required Information

items: Printer information (what printers they have access to)
CMD for: Hostname (existing PC name) and whoami (User login details)
Ask the user for their password

blocks.text: Backup Important User Data

Export bookmarks and saved passwords and save them temporarily to desktop, documents, or OneDrive. Check if files are in Downloads as well and copy them to desktop/documents/OneDrive as necessary. Desktop/Documents usually do not need manual backup but always verify before assuming data is server-synced.
Check Folder Redirection / Offline Files
Determine whether folders are available offline. If necessary, contact the office to configure offline files properly.
AFTER INFORMATION IS COLLECTED

Once all information and backups are complete, either remove PC from DOMAIN. This way AD stays clean or rename it if PC gets repurposed. Power off the old PC and install/power on the new PC. If replacing a laptop, it may be easier to leave the old one running temporarily for reference.
STEP 2 – ADD PC TO THE DOMAIN
Login
Login to the domain controller (CHG-PDC2025) under your CSI-NAME account. If you require the Csupport credentials, feel free to ask your immediate supervisor/manager.
Renaming the PC and Joining the Domain.
Go to This PC -> Properties -> Domain or Workgroup -> Change and enter the domain name. In this case, it is CHGOLF. This will require a restart and the server administrator credentials.
The naming convention for CHG has been mixed until Club Support has taken over from the previous IT provider. Our own naming convention is as follows:
CHG-[FirstInitial][First3LettersOfLastName]-[MonthYearOfSetUp]
For example, if you set up a workstation for John Doe on July 2026, the device name will be:
CHG-JDoe-0726
STEP 3 – ADD PRINTERS
Method 1 – From Server
Install printers directly from \\CHG-PDC2025
Method 2 – Windows Printer Settings
Navigate to Settings -> Printers and dd printers manually if necessary.
Some printers require manufacturer drivers, make sure to print test pages if unsure which printer is correct and to test connections.
STEP 4 – REMOTE DESKTOP / WORK FROM HOME
Enable RDP

While logged into the CSupport account on the new device, navigate to Remote Desktop settings and enable RDP access. Allow the user's account to remote into the PC and verify that RDP permissions are enabled for their account.
To create the shortcut, enter Remote Desktop Connection, input the device IP address (from CMD -> ipconfig) and save the RDP shortcut to the desktop.
VPN Setup
Currently CHG uses SonicWall as their VPN, so refer to the separate guide for the complete setup. Once that’s finished, test the VPN by:
Connecting laptop to a hotspot
Starting the VPN
Login with user credentials
If VPN setup fails, uninstall WAN Miniports in Device Manager, reboot the device, and retry.
STEP 5 – USER ACCOUNT CONFIGURATION
Taskbar Cleanup

Change the taskbar settings in Settings -> Personalization -> Taskbar Settings and adjust taskbar preferences, including changing the search icon, removing the weather/current news popup on the left, and aligning the icons to the left or center.
Make sure to remove the unnecessary icons such as 365 Copilot and pin the necessary ones, such as Chrome, Adobe, Word, etc.
Set Default Applications
Configure defaults such as Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.
Install Additional Applications

Install any non-standard applications required by the user. Some applications require admin rights. Adobe Creative Cloud should be installed under the CSupport account. Obtain the Northstar POS link (if required).
(Add camera installation)
Microsoft Account Sign-In
Have the user sign into Microsoft services  and complete MFA setup if required .
Final Data Restore
Re-add printers if needed, restore Downloads folder contents, and import browser bookmarks/passwords into the preferred browser.
Install SentinelOne and TeamViewer

SentinelOne requires an installation package from K2, while Teamviewer can be installed thorugh the Club Support website. Go to the website, then Client Support, then scroll down to install TeamViewer. Make sure to set the password to the standard Club Support password!
Remove Bloat

Depending on the original model of the new workstation/laptop, there will be most likely be some bloatware left on the device. As the admin account, disable UAC and uninstall unnecessary programs that were left over during the installation.
ADAPTED FROM WORKSTATION SETUP, DOUBLE CHECK IF THIS WORKSTATION
Enable RDP

While logged into the CSupport account on the new device, navigate to Remote Desktop settings and enable RDP access. Allow the user's account to remote into the PC and verify that RDP permissions are enabled for their account.
To create the shortcut, enter Remote Desktop Connection, input the device IP address (from CMD -> ipconfig) and save the RDP shortcut to the desktop.
VPN Setup
Currently CHG uses SonicWall as their VPN, so refer to the separate guide for the complete setup. Once that’s finished, test the VPN by:
Connecting laptop to a hotspot
Starting the VPN
Login with user credentials
If VPN setup fails, uninstall WAN Miniports in Device Manager, reboot the device, and retry.
RDP Setup
Make sure you have/check
The user's office computer name/terminal server name or IP address (can be found in Atera)
VPN access  (for remote connection only)
Remote Desktop access enabled on the office computer and user has been added to the list of who can remotely access the PC (Check security groups!)
Sleep is disabled on the office computer
The user's username and password.
RDP Connection
Confirm the user is connected to the VPN
Verify the office or remote computer is online by pinging its computer name or IP address.
Open Remote Desktop Connection on the user’s home computer by pressing Windows Key + R, typing mstsc, and pressing Enter.
Enter the office computer name or terminal server name into Remote Desktop Connection.
Enter the user’s domain username and password when prompted.
Accept the security warning to continue connecting.
Once connected, verify the user can access their network drives, applications, cameras, and any other required resources.

Create a saved RDP shortcut by opening RDC, entering the server name and your username, clicking Show Options, choosing Save As, saving the .rdp file to your desktop, and later opening that file to launch the connection automatically.

Setup requires only the IP address and user credentials but user must be added to the “VPN Access” group in AD first.

Installing Printers on workstations
Find the name of the printer to be installed in the \\CHG-NSTAR2025 or \\CHG-PDC2025 server.
Make sure that the user has the relevant group membership for the printer to be used (Administration, Fitness, etc.).
In File Explorer, put \\CHG-NSTAR2025 or \\CHG-PDC2025 into the File Explorer and this should bring up a list of all printers that are available to the user account.
Find the printer to be installed and double-click it to automatically install the printer drivers.
Send a test print to the printer in Settings to verify its connectivity.
